sentences.text: Kronosaurus is considered one of the largest known pliosaurs.
Initial estimates based on the Harvard skeleton suggested Kronosaurus could reach around 13 meters in length, but later revisions placed its size between 9 and more than 10 meters long.
The largest identified skulls of Kronosaurus are larger than those of the largest known theropod dinosaurs.
Its large cone-shaped teeth indicate it likely ate large prey, and the flippers of the largest representatives would have spanned more than 5 meters.
The genus Kronosaurus was formally described by Albert Heber Longman in 1924.
A partial marine reptile fossil was sent to the Queensland Museum in 1899 on behalf of Andrew Crombie, becoming the holotype cataloged as QM F1609.
This first known specimen was received by a museum in 1899.
Fossil evidence suggests Kronosaurus was an apex predator that preyed on sea turtles and other plesiosaurs in the Eromanga Sea, where water temperatures were close to freezing.
The type species of the genus Kronosaurus is Kronosaurus queenslandicus.
Eiectus longmani is listed as a possible synonym of Kronosaurus queenslandicus in a 2022 study.
Phylogenetic studies since 2013 place Kronosaurus within the subfamily Brachaucheninae.
Kronosaurus lived in what is now Australia during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
Fossils cataloged as QM F2137 come from the Toolebuc Formation and date to the Albian stage.
A specimen initially attributed to Kronosaurus dates from the Upper Aptian of the Paja Formation in Colombia.
Romer ordered the addition of plaster to incomplete bones during the restoration, a decision that complicates access to real fossils.
It is suggested that the Harvard skeleton was reconstructed with incorrect proportions, with Colin McHenry arguing the specimen has eight extra vertebrae and an incorrectly shaped sagittal crest.
Many researchers advocate using CT scans to analyze the real fossils due to the plaster restoration issues.
